course_notes: (Same as AAS 385W 1, ANT 385W 2) This class will explore and engage the histories, experiences, and political movements that have shaped the Black Atlantic world. Over the course of the semester, we will examine the origins of anti-Black racism and injustice in the Atlantic slave trade and African colonization. We will then interrogate more recent structures and experiences of racial oppression and inequality as well as the struggles for justice within Black communities that have emerged in response. We will also explore questions of historical memory and the case for reparations. Case studies will include Ghana, Jamaica, the United Kingdom, France, and the United States. In addition, students will have the opportunity to choose their own case studies to research for their final papers.
